subject: POC Trial Planning - workload & success criteria (follow-up)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anne Wu <anne.wu@acmehealth.com>, Carlos Ramirez <carlos.ramirez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - Acme Health POC

Thanks Anne - great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the trial kick-off:

Summary (from today's discovery)
- Primary goal: validate latency and cost for 1-2 critical workflows (clinical triage assistant + patient message summarization)
- Success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 200ms (in-region) for inference path; summary quality >= baseline human-rated score (TBD); cost target <= $X per 1k requests (we'll refine)
- Timeline: 4-week POC (kickoff next Monday 5/24) with two evaluation checkpoints (end of week 1 and week 3)

Proposed evaluation plan & ownership
- Redwood (Ben/Marissa): provide dedicated trial environment, baseline model variants, and run synthetic workload based on your profile. Deliverables: weekly runbook, perf dashboards, and a short write-up at each checkpoint.
- Acme Health (Anne/Carlos): provide workload profile (RPS, token length distributions, concurrency, burst patterns), production sample prompts, and a list of 5-10 representative test cases for human quality review.

Immediate next steps (action items)
1) Anne: share workload traffic profile + any constraints by EOD Thursday (5/20) - sample CSV or bullet list works.
2) Ben: send MoP and POC timeline doc (attached) and schedule kickoff.
3) Marissa/Dylan: prep perf test harness and expected metric dashboard.

Attachments: acmehealth-poc-mop-v1.pdf, poc-timeline.xlsx

If that aligns, I'll schedule the kickoff and loop in infra for VPN/KMS notes.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Anne Wu <anne.wu@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Ramirez <carlos.ramirez@acmehealth.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - Acme Health POC

Thanks Ben - appreciate the clear recap. High level confirms. A few clarifying Qs before we send the workload csv:
- For latency target, is the 95th percentile measured at your hosted endpoint (us-west) or at our private deployment (we're considering private due to PHI)?
- For the quality baseline, we can provide the 5 test cases. Do you have a simple rubric you prefer for the human-rated score?

We'll push a first-cut workload profile by EOD Thursday. Quick heads-up on traffic shape:
- Typical steady-state: ~8 RPS across the triage endpoint during business hours (PST)
- Peak bursts: short spikes up to 60 RPS for 30-90s during morning summary windows
- Token lengths: average prompt 120 tokens, summary target ~60 tokens; worst-case prompt up to 600 tokens for long notes
- Concurrency: expected 12 concurrent requests for triage, 30 for batch summarization job runs

Is there a preferred CSV schema you want for the profile?

--
Anne
Director of AI Product, Acme Health
anne.wu@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anne Wu <anne.wu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - Acme Health POC

Great - thanks for the early traffic notes, that's very helpful. Quick answers:
- Latency measurement: we can run both. For hosted endpoints we'll measure at the edge (us-west) end-to-end; for Private deployment we measure inside the VPC. We'll propose targets per-deployment in the MoP.
- Quality rubric: we'll attach a simple 3-point rubric (Acceptable / Some Issues / Fail) that reviewers can use - will include in the deliverables.

Preferred CSV schema (simple): columns: endpoint, time_window, rps_avg, rps_peak, burst_duration_s, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_response_tokens, concurrency_expected, notes
Example row: triage, business_hours, 8, 60, 90, 120, 60, 12, "short spikes at 08:30-09:00 PST"

If that works, please send the CSV and sample prompts. We'll ingest and turn around an initial perf run by Friday (5/21).

Also cc'ing Marissa and Dylan to start capacity planning.

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Anne Wu <anne.wu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - Acme Health POC

Quick infra notes from our side:
- For bursts up to 60 RPS with 600-token prompts, we'll likely recommend a dedicated small pool with autoscale headroom. Please include the peak distribution (how many bursts per hour/day).
- Token accounting: long prompts (600 tokens) have higher cost and KV cache implications - please flag the percent of those in your CSV.
- If you're trying Private, we'll need VPN access details and a point of contact for infra. Otherwise hosted will be faster to get started.

Action: Anne, if you can include "percent_long_prompts" and "burst_count_per_hour" fields in the CSV that will let us size the GPU pool and batching windows more accurately.

Thanks - Marissa
Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Ramirez <carlos.ramirez@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Anne Wu <anne.wu@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - Acme Health POC

Hi team - attaching a quick CSV (see Drive link) and a short sample of prompts; copying a few numbers inline as well:
- endpoint, time_window, rps_avg, rps_peak, burst_duration_s, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_response_tokens, concurrency_expected, percent_long_prompts, burst_count_per_hour
- triage, business_hours, 8, 60, 90, 120, 60, 12, 5, 2
- summarization_batch, nightly, 0.5, 30, 600, 450, 200, 30, 20, 1

We uploaded acme-poc-workload-v1.csv to the Drive folder. Let us know if you want CSV changes. Looking forward to Friday's perf run.

Thanks,
Carlos
